generator: the binaries under fixtures/locations/ are written by scripts/gen_location_fixtures.py
fictional: EVERY coordinate in this artefact and in the files it pins is INVENTED — points in open ocean, chosen so no fixture can disclose a real household location.
rules: LOCATION READ (app/services/location.py). Images: the GPS IFD (0x8825) of the RAW EXIF payload, taken the way services/capture.py takes it — im.info['exif'] for JPEG/HEIF, the eXIf chunk walker for PNG, tag_v2 for TIFF — and parsed with Image.Exif().load(raw) then get_ifd(0x8825), so no path decodes a pixel. GPSLatitude/GPSLongitude are 1 to 3 rationals (degrees[, minutes[, seconds]]); GPSLatitudeRef/GPSLongitudeRef decide the sign, S and W negating, a missing ref reading as N/E. A zero denominator, a NaN, a magnitude out of range (|lat| > 90, |lon| > 180) or exactly (0, 0) is NO location. Videos: com.apple.quicktime.location.ISO6709 from moov/meta (keys + ilst) first, else ©xyz from moov/udta (a QuickTime text atom: 2-byte length, 2-byte language, then the string); both are ISO 6709 decimal, ±DD.DDDD±DDD.DDDD[±alt][CRS]/, the altitude and any CRS suffix ignored. location_source is 'exif' or 'quicktime' when a location was read, 'none' when the file was read and carried none, 'unreadable' when the original could not be read at all (retryable). A coordinate reaches Postgres and GET /api/map/markers and nothing else — no log line, no derived tier, print, poster or transcoded video, no other API body.

jpeg-north-east.jpg.note: N/E refs, whole degrees and minutes.

jpeg-south-west.jpg.note: S/W refs negate the same magnitudes — the sign rule.

jpeg-no-gps.jpg.note: no GPS IFD at all: read, and no location.

jpeg-null-island.jpg.note: exactly (0,0) — the no-fix value, never a photograph.

jpeg-zero-denominator.jpg.note: rationals with a zero denominator (NaN), and no ZeroDivisionError.

jpeg-missing-refs.jpg.note: no ref tags → north and east, the EXIF default.

png-exif-after-idat.png.note: the eXIf chunk sits AFTER IDAT — invisible to the header parse, and getexif() would decode the pixels.

tiff-gps.tif.note: a TIFF's GPS IFD lives in its own first IFD (tag_v2).

heic-gps.heic.note: HEIC carries the same EXIF payload as a JPEG.

mov-iso6709.mov.note: com.apple.quicktime.location.ISO6709 under moov/meta, WITH an altitude component.

mp4-xyz.mp4.note: ©xyz under moov/udta — a QuickTime text atom, not a data sub-box.
